doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Trips to Los Angeles and Europe to find musicians
summary: He made three trips to Los Angeles for older black musicians, beyond the Central Avenue Sounds project, plus visits to France and Holland.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You know I think I’m probably spoiled in the job that I’ve been able to do in that I don’t have to work nearly as hard gathering interviews as I think some people do, and probably yourself. What lengths have you gone to, can you think of a couple of instances where you’ve really gone to super human efforts?

Well I’ve certainly gone over to the continent with a very specific desire to locate certain people. I mean it’s not super human but I’ve had three trips to Los Angeles specifically to get the older black guys because that’s a particular area of interest. Following on from this moment with Darensbourg, I spent a lot of time in Los Angeles with Joe when we were starting to get all the material for this together, and that exposed me to a whole scene over there, you know that’s been to some extent documented by Central Avenue Sounds and Stephen A. — what’s his name — Isoardi.

Anyway, the guy who has managed that program. But there are still guys I got to that they never did and I’ve actually still got those interviews. I mean in that sense yes, you are getting into some trouble. You’re getting into the black area of Los Angeles, you know you’re not too sure how easy that’s going to be, and I suppose that would come up too. It’s not super human, but at least an out of the ordinary effort. And I say going over to France, going over to Holland where I’ve certainly been to see key American musicians who are living there, that sort of thing.
